category_specific_evidence: Commit and PR#19944: bdtrik(0.0, inf, 1.0) (binomial distribution with infinite number of events) hung indefinitely; the fix returns NaN when the number of events/support is infinite.

Diff to _cdflib_wrappers.pxd: in bdtrik and nbdtrik the guard changed from isnan(xn) to not isfinite(xn), so infinite xn returns NAN immediately. Special values involved: +inf for xn; nan for p, xn and pr.

Test test_bdtrik_nbdtrik_inf asserts sp.bdtrik and sp.nbdtrik return NaN for infinite xn across y and p inputs including nan, -inf, -10, -1, 0, 1e-5, 0.5, 0.9999, 1.0, 10, inf (y) and nan, -inf, -10, -1, 0, 1e-5, 0.5, 1.0, inf (p), using exact np.isnan assertions.

Discussion: previously these functions returned garbage in these cases; bdtrik(0, inf, 1) previously returned infinity and then hung; maintainers agreed NaN is the correct return and suggested an iteration upper bound.
